messages.subject: Neuralnetwork and Keras issues
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to test the tutorial  of Keras for neural network as demonstrated in a video. I strictly followed the steps as below:
library(keras)
library(mlbench)
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)
library(neuralnet)
# data
data("BostonHousing")
data<-BostonHousing
str(data)
# data %>% mutate_if(is.factor, as.numeric) # if there is more than one vector
str(data)
data$chas = as.numeric(data$chas)
str(data)
## Neural network visualization
n<-neuralnet(medv~., data = data,
             hidden =c(10, 5), linear.output = F,
             lifesign = 'full', rep = 1)
plot(n, col.hidden = 'darkgreen',
     show.weights = F,
     information = F,
     fill = 'lightblue')
# Matrix
data<-as.matrix(data)
dimnames(data)<-NULL
#partition
set.seed(1234)
ind <- sample(2, nrow(data), replace=T, prob = c(0.7, 0.3))
training <- data[ind==1, 1:13]
test<- data[ind==2, 1:13]
trainingTarget <- data[ind==1, 14]
testTarget <- data[ind==2, 14]
#normalization
m<-colMeans(training)
s<-apply(training, 2, sd)
training <- scale(training, center = m, scale = s)
test <- scale(test, center = m, scale = s)
# create model
model <- keras_model_sequential()
I could not proceed from here as I have got following error:

model <- keras_model_sequential()
Error: parse error: trailing garbage
          hesh\\Documents\\.condarc" } Using Anaconda Cloud api site h
                     (right here) ------^

Do you have any idea about it?

Thanks

--

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Neuralnetwork and Keras issues
parts:
The sessionInfo() part is just to let us all know what your computing
environment is. You might, for instance, be using an obsolete version
of R or of some relevant package. That doesn't seem to be the case
here, but if it were, the easy fix would be to tell you to update R
and/or the package.

Regarding spaces in file names, let me give an example. My base
directory for my R documents is:

/home/mike/Documents/R

I *could* make a different directory, call it:

My Documents

such that my base directory for R would be:

/home/mike/My Documents/R

That path name has a space in it (between "My" and "Documents").
That's perfectly OK from the point of view of the file system in
general, but it may be that a given R package would parse that as:

/home/mike/My

plus some "garbage" at the end:

Documents/R

I'm not saying that *is* your problem, just that the error message you
posted resembles that kind of message.
